Guys, please do yourself a favor and download Dxvk plugin for this game. It's a Vulkan translation layer that has the potential to double your framerate. Yes, a program meant for Linux-to-Vulkan api makes GTA IV, a non-Vulkan game, run better on Windows - that's what a disaster this games coding is. 
You simply download dxvk, go into the x32 folder located in the zip file and then cut/copy d3d9.dll and dxgi.dll and put them into your GTA IV directory (where the games .exe is located) 
My game is now a stable 60fps 90% of the time with all high settings and I'm one of those scrubs on a decade old AMD 8350. I do adaptive V-sync via the Nvidia Control Panel, for what it's worth. The only downside, if you even use it, is that it disables the Steam overlay, but the Rockstar one remains active: so you'll still see your delicious achievements pop when you get them. 

Also, if your game is stuck at only recognizing 512mb of Vram - an old issue I thought was fixed but is apparently back thanks to Rockstars general incompetence and apathy - simply add a commandline via Steam in the launch options for the game with your Vram amount. 
For example, "-availablevidmem 8192" if you have 8GB of Vram on your GPU. 

It's hard to recommend this game without these improvements but once you get it running smoothly, you won't be disappointed. It's a travesty that we - as the consumer - have to jump through hoops and essentially do Rockstars job to make this game work well but those clowns have become a straight parody of themselves ever since GTA V online started making them half a billion a year. They've literally become one of the companies they would satirize in a GTA game, requiring their own customers to effectively do their programming just to make their game run adequately. It's frankly disgusting but welcome to the video game industry in 2021. 

Alright, rant over. I genuinely hope this helps you as it helped me because everyone deserves to experience this gem of a game free of issues.

UPDATE: FusionFix is also a must use mod and, with the newest update, now includes DXVK built into it. So you can toggle between Vulkan and DX9 right from the GTA IV graphics menu with the newest version of Fusion Fix installed, skipping the steps I listed above. Fusion Fix also includes hundreds of other fixes and improvements for this game, from volumetric fog to being able to choose between Xbox or PS button prompts. It's a must.

The game is still on Steam, but the ability to purchase it has been removed. A spokesperson from Rockstar explains why:

"Grand Theft Auto 4 was originally created for the Games For Windows Live platform. With Microsoft no longer supporting Games For Windows Live, it is no longer possible to generate the additional keys needed to continue selling the current version of the game," a Rockstar representative said. "We are looking at other options for distributing GTA4 for PC and will share more information as soon as we can."The game is still on Steam, but the ability to purchase it has been removed.

GTA IV holds a special place among open-world games. Its story is deep, the characters are compelling, and Liberty City’s atmosphere is amazing. I definitely recommend buying and playing it! I started this year on my Steam Deck, and it runs really well with no FPS issues. I just finished the story for the first time in 2025, and even though the game is quite old, it’s still incredible.

“The American Dream comes with a body count.”

This is Rockstar’s most mature, most honest game. There’s no Vinewood, no satire. Just Liberty City, dark and cold, pulsing with corruption and concrete.

Niko Bellic isn’t flashy. He’s haunted. A war veteran trying to wash off blood with more blood. The story is heavy, the weight of consequence never lets up. Choices sting. Death has meaning. You feel the loneliness in every call Roman makes.

The city feels alive but suffocating. Grit replaces glamour.
The radio, the voice acting, the physics, It's unreal. Car chases hurt, shootouts feel raw, and friendships? They matter here.

It’s a tragedy disguised as a sandbox.
And it’s one of the best stories ever told in gaming.

Hi... I am writing this review after playing for over 100 hours, and I can confidently say that GTA IV has the best story in the entire GTA franchise. I loved the game so much that I grinded out 100% of the Steam achievements.

Everyone should play this masterpiece at least once to see what Rockstar cooked up before GTA V. However, if you are playing on a modern PC, there are a few things you need to know:

1. DOWNLOAD FUSIONFIX:
Before you even start the game, download the FusionFix mod pack. The original PC port is notoriously broken on modern hardware. If you play with an uncapped framerate (anything above 60 FPS), the game engine physically breaks. Quick-time events fail, minigames (like the dancing in the DLC) become impossible to beat, and the final mission can permanently soft-lock. FusionFix patches these engine bugs, fixes the lighting, and gives you a smooth, glitch-free experience.

2. THE DLCs ARE MANDATORY:
Just completing the base game with Niko is not enough. You absolutely need to play the two included DLC episodes (The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony). They aren't just extra missions; they contain massive, overlapping stories that directly connect to the main game. Playing all three campaigns is the only way to experience the complete story of Liberty City.

3. THE DRIVING PHYSICS:
Be prepared for the driving to feel very different if you are coming from GTA V. The cars here are heavy and have realistic suspension. It takes an hour or two to get used to, but once you master it, the car chases are some of the most satisfying in the series.

100% highly recommended. If you love open-world games with gritty, deep narratives, this is an absolute must-play.

I saw people saying that had too download all these various files and thought it too much of a hassle. Plus the games for windows that seemed to have everyone up in arms. I run a windows 10 machine which can easily run GTA 5 so no hardware issues.

However I thought I'd give it a shot. 

I knew this was an older game and I would need to change the compatibility settings on the local folders applications. Easy for anyone to do. I set it to windows 7 mode and put it to run in administrative mode. This seemed to start up the game no issues, then I ran into the "apparently" broken games for windows part, which as you read the information displayed on the screen says you can play in offline, you just need to setup an offline profile, so no hassle there either. However I pressed on with online mode to see if it was possible to run, all that happened is it redirected me to xbox.account, which I believe is on most windows 10 PCs. A quick click and account made, games running. 

The only issue I faced was as the game was around prior to current graphics cards, it wouldn't recognise above 2GB cards. To a rather hilarious intro cut scene I saw floating items and diamonds etc with no characters visible, just floating hair. Everything else was visible apart from the map in the menu as well. A quick google and I found the answer. All I needed to do was change the launch options for the game in steam. To do this I right clicked on the game in steam and went into properties and advance launching options. I simple copy and pasted the following text

-nomemrestrict -norestrictions 

Into the text box and ran the game again. What the text does it tell the game to ignore its restrictions around available card usage. 

Everything was as I remember it use to be. This didn't require me to download any dll files, patches, fixes, cracks etc. Apparently some music is missing from the game due to licencing and there is a way to get it back in there if you really want it but I wont go into that here, all I can say is google is your friend. GTA IV as a game is considered one of the best games of all time for a reason. For the time it was a mind blowing leap in graphics and in physics, and it still holds up in 2026. Female peds actually fight back too.

The physics in the game are over the top but crazy fun to play around with. Euphoria's implementation in this game is still top tier and never makes the game boring, and I wish more games used NaturalMotion's Euphoria. I'm currently doing a full playthrough of every GTA game in anticipation of GTA VI, and out of all of them, GTA IV was the one I was looking forward to revisiting the most. I had already poured more than 200 hours into it back in 2008, but somehow I never came back to it after that.

The day GTA IV launched is still burned into my memory...

I remember sitting in school, debating whether I should stay for the rest of the day or head home after the very first class. It didn't take long to make up my mind. I slipped out of school like it was a side mission straight out of Bully, caught the bus home, and couldn't stop thinking about the adventure that was waiting for me in Liberty City. Whatever punishment I was going to get later felt completely worth it.

Coming back all these years later reminded me why this game left such a lasting impression.

It's funny to call GTA IV "underrated" considering it has a Metacritic score of 98, but I genuinely think it doesn't get nearly enough appreciation today. Whenever people discuss Rockstar's greatest achievements, GTA IV often ends up overshadowed by some of their other titles. I feell like that's a shame, because this game is one of the clearest examples of why Rockstar became the benchmark for open world games.

The level of detail is astonishing. During one mission you're tailing someone when your phone rings. If you let it ring, the target hears it, gets suspicious, and starts running. Put your phone on silent beforehand, and he never notices, you can simply hang up and continue following him. Friends and acquaintances react to how you drive. Some enjoy reckless speeding, others prefer you obey traffic laws. Some even have favorite radio stations, and playing the music they like actually improves your relationship with them. These aren't features the game constantly points out. They're simply there, quietly making the world feel believable.

They even created a fully functional in game internet packed with thousands of browseable pages, making Liberty City feel incredibly alive. Rockstar have always been masters at integrating the internet and social media into their worlds, and it makes me even more excited to see what they'll do with GTA VI.

And that's what GTA IV does better than almost any other open-world game. Liberty City doesn't just feel alive, it feels like a character of its own. People jog through the parks. A lone saxophone player fills the streets with music. Shuttle buses and taxis carry travelers to the airport terminals. Every neighborhood feels inhabited by people living their own lives. It's a city that's constantly moving, yet somehow feels suffocating. Glamour is replaced by grime. It's cold, cynical, and yet so unforgettable.

The story is really exceptional. The main character Niko Bellic is a departure from previous protagonist in the series, he isn't a flashy action hero. He's a man haunted by his past, a war veteran who seemingly could do no right, trying to wash away blood with more blood. His search for a better life slowly becomes yet another cycle of violence, betrayal, and regret. Rockstar wasn't afraid to explore dark themes, and because of that, it feels like every major story beat has certain weight attached to it. Death has consequences. Loss lingers. Even just cruising past Liberty City without a cause makes you feel just how lonely Niko really is. To this day, I still consider it one of Rockstar's finest stories.

Important to say that this game also received two single player DLC's and The Ballad of Gay Tony deserves special mention. Even after all these years, it's still one of the best single-player expansions I've ever played, offering the perfect contrast to the darker tone of the main game.

GTA IV isn't just another open world crime game. It's a time capsule of 2008. A technical marvel for its era. A masterclass in environmental storytelling and world building. Nearly two decades later, Liberty City still feels more believable than many open worlds released today.

Some games age, but GTA IV....GTA IV simply waits for you to come back.

[h1] GREAT GAME, BROKEN PORT [/h1]

[b] TL;DR: [/b] Grand Theft Auto IV is a fantastic game. By many metrics, one could consider it a perfect game. Its' writing, world building, game mechanics, and physics are near flawless and years ahead of its' time. Unfortunately, as with many console games ported to PC, this game is extremely buggy. It is essentially unplayable without extensive modding. 

That's the basics. More details provided below for context.

This port was extremely broken upon launch. One of the most cited issues since has been poor optimization, for which the response from Rockstar at the time was that "higher settings are provided for future generations of PCs with higher specifications than are currently widely available." Indeed, as hardware improved over the years, so did performance. Unfortunately, as with many games, GTA IV's physics are tied to framerate. Since the game was designed to run at approximately 30 frames per second, there are several mechanics of the game that break entirely when the game exceeds 30 FPS. These are including, but not limited to:

-Real-time cutscenes (severe physical stuttering and camera zoom)
-Mission essential timers
-NPC AI / pathfinding
-Vehicle physics (turning, braking, sliding, etc)
-Various minigames (e.g. TLAD's arm-wrestling)
-Various mission-essential Quick Time Events (the very last mission of the game cannot be completed)

Ultimately, the game's engine was not never properly adapted for modern hardware. This means, in addition to the aforementioned issues, you will also deal with these issues:

-Ineffective utilization of CPU cores (even more CPU bottleneck)
-Inefficient VRAM detection (forcing lower quality textures and reduced draw distances) 
-Improper VSync implementation (screen tearing at high refresh rates and audio stuttering)

Long story short, the game is completely unplayable without mods. So let's talk about how you can go about doing Rockstar's job for them. First, since Rockstar's occasional handful of patches did nothing but break several essential mods, you'll need to use a tool to downgrade the game to a previous version that will work with essential mods that haven't been updated. Once that's done, you'll need to find the specific mods you need (such as FusionFIx, OpenIV, etc.) Of course, several of these mods can conflict, meaning you'll either need to spend several hours modifying the files, or finding the specific versions that run together (for example, FusionFix version 1.10 is the only version that doesn't conflict with DXVK and ZMenu on game version 10.0.7.0,) Now that you've finished your doctorate in aerospace engineering, you can finally play the game. Provided you keep the game locked to 60 FPS, you shouldn't have any more issues. 

My point in discussing this ad nauseam is that you shouldn't have to do all of this work just to play a PC port. This is a extremely beloved and influential game that has sold millions of copies worldwide. And yet, Rockstar has made no effort to fix this game on PC. They've remastered and rereleased nearly every other game in the series. Yet, even with Grand Theft Auto IV's recent cultural resurgence, it appears that Rockstar is concerned with more pressing matters, like milking GTA Online to death, releasing a $60 broken "remastered" GTA Trilogy port, and... *checks notes* porting Red Dead Redemption to Netflix. I really fucking wish I was joking.

This game has a very active community, and high quality mods are still being released. If you've played the game enough and want to experiment with new modded content, go for it. If you haven't played it, you should probably just play it on console. If you don't have a console, go get an Xbox 360 off Ebay or something. Playing Grand Theft Auto IV for the first time on this abysmal dogshit port is something I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy.

Fantastic game, even in 2023. Tips for new players in 2023:

1) GSHADE: Install GShade and choose DXVK/Vulkan. Free performance uplift for any semi-modern GPU.
2) DOWNGRADE RADIO: Use the community downgrade patch (google it) to restore the game to 1.0.8 or lower. (1.0.8 or 7 are most popular). This restores older radio stations. Choose Old Vladivostok Radio if asked.
2a) EFLC RADIO LIMIT: Optionally, install the mod to limit the Episodes/DLC radio to their own episodes. This helps keep the tone of the main story from changing early on with pop and dance music drowning out the Vladivostok Russian radio.
Optional easy enhancements:
3) TIMECYCLE: Install a Timecycle mod of your choice (I use Sweet Autumn). There cost 0 performance, and go well with Reshade's expanded color space. (Timecycles control weather/color/tone at all times of day.)
4) RESHADE RTGI: If your system can handle it, go subscribe to Pascal Glitcher's patreon for a month and grab an older release of his RTGI shader for Reshade and install it into Gshade. (I find 0.17 has the best performance. Newer versions look better but hurt the GPU more.). This can cost 5fps or so depending on the system, but adds immense depth to scenes.

Long version:
For best performance, you want to upgrade from DirectX 9 to Vulkan. Vulkan is massively faster than DX9, and the speedboost helps the game engine run at a solid 60fps without stutters, even when loading. Riding in a Taxi is instant teleportation on a good system. You can do this via a project called DXVK. It's as simple as dropping it into the game folder. DXVK can be setup via a DXVK.conf file (set maximum resolution here) and one of these settings allows you to enable true HDR by expanding the HDR color range. But wait, it gets better: Reshade offers modern post processing effects, but some of the more advanced effects in Reshade (as of January 2023) don't all work great with Vulkan in DXVK. 

Enter Gshade. Gshade is a fork (variant) of Reshade, which has a slightly different Vulkan implementation than Reshade which works great with GTAIV. It also releases with a integrated DXVK version. So you get Gshade/Vulkan in one install. At a later time, Reshade may operate just as well, but at the time of writing Gshade was far more consistent in being able to offer depth effects in GTAIV. I use a light DOF, light bloom, levels (to expand the color range to full blacks), and RTGI 0.17.

From there, you have GShade and Vulkan, and if you have used the downgrade patch, you have your game with original radios on 1.0.7 or 8. Now you can add a few community fixes (2DFX, FusionFix and ZolikaPatch) for the 1.0.7/8 releases, and suddenly your game is looking insanely good and running at a consistent 60fps+ with no frame pacing issues. Note: In ZolikaPatch, disable the "quick startup" and "vram" and "memory manangement" hacks, as these actually slow down DXVK.

Timecycles are far more powerful than they sound. The timecycles alone, with no other mods, allow you to change the color grading, effects, and lighting of the in-game appearance drastically, with no external tools. The default game timecycles are meant to give a smoggy, grungy filter on the city. This is fine, but if you want to use other post processing, something a bit less heavy might be better. I use Sweet Autumn.

"But what about ENBs or mods"
This is up to you. Personally, I think an ENBs 5-10 years ago offered unparalleled enhancements and would strongly recommend it. But with how far the Reshade project has come, frankly there's not a ton that ENB offers that a good Reshade+Timecycle mod does not nowadays, and Timecycle mods are much easier to implement.

Guys, please do yourself a favor and download Dxvk plugin for this game. It's a Vulkan translation layer that has the potential to double your framerate. Yes, a program meant for Linux-to-Vulkan api makes GTA IV, a non-Vulkan game, run better on Windows - that's what a disaster this games coding is.
You simply download dxvk, go into the x32 folder located in the zip file and then cut/copy d3d9.dll and dxgi.dll and put them into your GTA IV directory (where the games .exe is located)
My game is now a stable 60fps 90% of the time with all high settings and I'm one of those scrubs on a decade old AMD 8350. I do adaptive V-sync via the Nvidia Control Panel, for what it's worth. The only downside, if you even use it, is that it disables the Steam overlay, but the Rockstar one remains active: so you'll still see your delicious achievements pop when you get them.

Also, if your game is stuck at only recognizing 512mb of Vram - an old issue I thought was fixed but is apparently back thanks to Rockstars general incompetence and apathy - simply add a commandline via Steam in the launch options for the game with your Vram amount.
For example, "-availablevidmem 8192" if you have 8GB of Vram on your GPU.

It's hard to recommend this game without these improvements but once you get it running smoothly, you won't be disappointed. In my opinion, one of the best Grand Theft Autos made.

Story:

To be honest, story-wise, this is by far my favorite Grand Theft Auto. The characters, the atmosphere, and the backstory all blend together to make a great story. I like the story a lot more than GTA V, because I feel like there's more substance to the game. Niko Bellic is not a bad person on the inside. He's a tortured soul that's been through a lot, and the only reason he does what he does is to stay alive so he can make it out of the pits that he was forced into. in GTA V, it's really just another heist story that doesn't exactly have a deep plot. Also, I'm a sucker for mafia stories, and no GTA has done the whole mob story scheme better than GTA IV.

Gameplay/Physics:

Gameplay-wise, this is also probably my favorite out of all the Grand Theft Autos, primarily because it seems the most realistic out of all the games. The only thing that I could see people complaining about is the way that cars handle in this game, but honestly after a while it's really fun once you get the hang of it (This is coming from a guy who loves drift racing games. If you hate drifting, you're gonna hate the driving in this game) The car physics are amazing. The crumple points are super realistic compared to GTA V. Even the sound effects when you hit another car is super realistic. (I've been in a car accident before, and I've seen them happen, I know the sound.) The combat is also fantastic. This is the only GTA where the combat feels almost real. The AI is a lot smarter than in GTA V. When you shoot an enemy, they don't just flinch, they look like they actually got hit. They'll drop, they'll stagger backwards, they'll fall over, they'll put their hand where they just got shot. Much of the time enemies will limp away if you get them to the lowest health. In GTA V it seems a lot more like any other third person shooter, where they just flinch for a second and get up and start shooting again.

Multiplayer (and arguably the driving) is the only thing I can say GTA V did better, but if it had the physics and gameplay of GTA IV, you would instantly have the best GTA possible. The main problem with the GTA IV Multiplayer is that it just feels kinda pointless, you don't really work towards anything.

The only con that I can give this game for the PC is the fact that you need Windows Live to play it. I have never liked Windows Live, and I find it stupid that I'm forced to use it. However, that can't stop me from giving this game a positive review, because this really is one of my favorite games ever created.

This game is a wonderful time capsule from 2008. That includes the political and economic climate at the time, the "brown grey and realistic" aesthetic, as well as the PC port quality (which is abysmal and requires third party fixes to run at modern standards). Rockstar still had something to prove when they were making this one. 

Whether it's better than GTA V or not is debatable, and people do, but I personally think it's the best game in the series. With fusionfix and the radio downgrader that restores cut songs from the soundtrack, this game provides an experience that no other game can. This was Rockstar's first ever attempt at making a game that nobody else was able to at a time when everybody and their mother were still trying to make a clone of the older GTA classics that had already taken the world by storm. Almost 20 years later, I don't think any other game dev has managed to even get close to matching its quality. Many have tried, but nobody paid attention to the little things more than 2008 Rockstar did.

It loses a lot of features from San Andreas, which many people (myself included) considered a major downgrade at the time, but it offers an unforgettable story, amazing fictional version of NYC, ridiculous but still entirely believable characters, and the best physics for combat and driving that still haven't been matched to this day except for RDR1. I put many, many more hours into GTA V and their other games, but IV goes for quality over quantity every step of the way.

Tons of people complain about the driving physics, but they're the reason I constantly return to this game. The sense of speed and the control you need to have border on racing sim territory compared to any other game of its type, and I spend most of my time just racing around at max speed and crashing into stuff. Older muscle cars are made of steel and don't damage easily (but you're flying out the windshield), the new pop can aluminum ones crumple, old cars lack ABS, 4WD, FWD and RWD cars all handle entirely differently, and there's no artificial cap on the max speed the cars can go like in GTA V. The attention to every detail of the driving was a game changer. Never gets old. 

The Ballad of Gay Tony is also arguably one of the best game expansions ever made.

10/10, would reinstall and play every year again.

[BudgetedIV]
VehicleBudget =
